newsitem.title: USA: Heartport system used in quintuple bypass.
newsitem.headline: Heartport system used in quintuple bypass.

text.p: Heartport Inc said Tuesday its minimally invasive heart surgery system was used for the first time in a quintuple bypass operation.

The company said a surgeon in Texas used the system to perform the five-vessel bypass opertion with just a 4-1/2 inch incision into the chest. Since the system was launched in January, it has been used in more than 1,000 heart surgeries, but had not previously been used in a quintuple bypass.

The company said doctors using the Heartport system can access the heart through the small incision and turn it around so to reach all sides. During surgery, catheters that are normally put into the body through the chest are instead threaded through the groin and into the leg. The catheters are attached to a heart-lung machine that keep bood flowing through the body while the heart is stopped.
The company says the small incision made when the Heartport system is used compares with a 12 to 15 inch cut and a broken sternum bone required during conventional surgery.

It said the Texas patient who underwent the quintuple bypass using the Heartport system was in the hospital for three days, compared with an average stay of a week or more for patients having conventional surgery.
